text: Marcus Halloway said the coach was happy with the session.
expected: [ATHLETE] said the coach was happy with the session.
notes: Given name + surname in subject position. CORRECTED at Phase 8: the original expected output also replaced the bare role noun 'the coach' with [COACH], which contradicted negative_04 in this same file ('my Coach' must survive, because a role is not an identity) and contradicted docs/ethics.md 5.1, which lists person NAMES for replacement, not role nouns. The name goes; the role stays.

text: I spoke to Coach Renner about the plan for Saturday.
expected: I spoke to [COACH] about the plan for Saturday.
notes: Title + surname. Weekday is NOT an identifier and must survive.

text: Nadia and I have trained together since we were juniors.
expected: [TEAMMATE] and I have trained together since we were juniors.
notes: Given name only, teammate role inferable from context.

text: Everyone calls him Bulldozer but his real name is Tomas Vrbik.
expected: Everyone calls him [PERSON] but his real name is [PERSON].
notes: Nickname plus a Central European surname. NER commonly misses nicknames.

text: I'm up against Okonkwo-Bright in the semi and she has never lost to me.
expected: I'm up against [OPPONENT] in the semi and she has never lost to me.
notes: Hyphenated surname, opponent role.

text: my physio jen keeps telling me to rest the shoulder
expected: my physio [PERSON] keeps telling me to rest the shoulder
notes: Lowercase name in informal text. Casing-dependent NER fails here.

text: Dr. Ellery Vance cleared me to compete this week.
expected: [PERSON] cleared me to compete this week.
notes: Honorific plus full name.

text: Someone tagged me as @quietstormruns in the post.
expected: Someone tagged me as [HANDLE] in the post.
notes: At-prefixed social handle.

text: My old username was k.mensah_07 before I changed it.
expected: My old username was [HANDLE] before I changed it.
notes: Handle with no @ prefix; dots and digits.

text: Send the schedule to t.abara@example-club.org before Friday.
expected: Send the schedule to [CONTACT] before Friday.
notes: Email address.

text: Call me on 07700 900412 if the warm-up slot moves.
expected: Call me on [CONTACT] if the warm-up slot moves.
notes: Phone number in an Ofcom reserved-for-drama range.

text: The draw is up at https://example-federation.test/draw/2026
expected: The draw is up at [URL]
notes: Full URL on a reserved .test TLD.

text: Northgate Harriers have been good to me this season.
expected: [TEAM] have been good to me this season.
notes: Club name.

text: My scholarship is through Wexholm Polytechnic and Brantley Sportswear.
expected: My scholarship is through [ORG] and [ORG].
notes: Institution plus sponsor in one sentence.

text: We fly to Karlsholm on Tuesday for the training camp.
expected: We fly to [LOCATION] on Tuesday for the training camp.
notes: Invented city. Weekday must survive.

text: The final is at the Verrick Street Arena, which I have never liked.
expected: The final is at the [LOCATION], which I have never liked.
notes: Named venue.

text: The Aldermere Invitational is the one I have been building towards.
expected: The [EVENT] is the one I have been building towards.
notes: Named competition.

text: I skipped the 2025 Coastal Series to focus on this block.
expected: I skipped the [EVENT] to focus on this block.
notes: Event edition including a year; the year goes with the event.

text: It all starts on 14 March 2026 and I am not ready.
expected: It all starts in [EVENT_WINDOW] and I am not ready.
notes: Exact date. docs/ethics.md 5.1 replaces exact dates with the relative time_to_competition field.

text: Three days out from the 06/09 final and the nerves are building.
expected: Three days out from the [EVENT_WINDOW] final and the nerves are building.
notes: Numeric date. The relative phrase 'three days out' MUST survive; it is contribution #3.

text: Wearing number 47 again after finishing fourth last year.
expected: Wearing [ID] again after finishing [ID] last year.
notes: Jersey number plus finishing position. docs/ethics.md 5.2: combinations re-identify.

text: As the only left-handed thrower in the national squad I stand out.
expected: As [ID] in the national squad I stand out.
notes: Uniqueness claim is itself an identifier even with no name present.

text: The nerves are bad this week. My ACL reconstruction still aches in the cold.
expected: The nerves are bad this week.
notes: Health detail is REMOVED ENTIRELY, not placeholdered (docs/ethics.md 5.1). Surrounding text survives.

text: I upped my sertraline dose before the trial and I felt flat all week.
expected: I felt flat all week.
notes: Medication is special-category data. P6 also makes health-subject text ineligible for the corpus at all.

text: Coach Renner told Marcus and me that Northgate Harriers want a result at the Aldermere Invitational.
expected: [COACH] told [TEAMMATE] and me that [TEAM] want a result at the [EVENT].
notes: Four identifier types in one sentence; tests interaction, not just detection.

text: dm me @halloway_m or email marcus@example-club.org, im at the Verrick Street Arena from monday
expected: dm me [HANDLE] or email [CONTACT], im at the [LOCATION] from monday
notes: Informal register, no capitalisation, three types. Weekday survives.

text: I keep thinking about all the ways this could go wrong.
expected: I keep thinking about all the ways this could go wrong.
notes: Pure construct language. Must be left untouched.

text: We fly out on Thursday and the heats are Saturday morning.
expected: We fly out on Thursday and the heats are Saturday morning.
notes: Weekdays are NOT identifiers. Over-redacting them destroys the temporal signal.

text: Mark my words, I will not let this one slip.
expected: Mark my words, I will not let this one slip.
notes: 'Mark' is a common given name here used as a verb. Classic NER false positive.

text: The Final is on Sunday and my Coach has the schedule.
expected: The Final is on Sunday and my Coach has the schedule.
notes: Capitalised common nouns with no proper name attached. 'my Coach' is a role, not an identity.

text: I finished the set in 47 seconds which is my best this block.
expected: I finished the set in 47 seconds which is my best this block.
notes: A number that is a performance measure, not a jersey number. Contrast with quasi_01.

text: Two days out and my legs feel heavy, but that is normal for me.
expected: Two days out and my legs feel heavy, but that is normal for me.
notes: Relative timing must survive de-identification. It is the contribution-3 field.

text: My stomach is in knots and my hands will not stop shaking.
expected: My stomach is in knots and my hands will not stop shaking.
notes: Body parts are somatic_anxiety evidence, not health data. Must not be stripped as 'health'.

text: The crowd in the north stand always gets to me.
expected: The crowd in the north stand always gets to me.
notes: Generic venue reference with no proper noun. Contrast with location_02.
